doc.title: Charles McPherson interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 12, 1998 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Moving to San Diego to be near his mother
summary: He lived in New York until about 1978, then moved to San Diego for his mother, married there, and travels for work.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: You were still living in New York?

Yeah, I lived in New York up until around 1978. And then I moved to San Diego. And the reason I moved was because my mom still lives here, and I’m an only child, she was getting on in age and I thought I should be with her and hang out with her. So I actually came out just with the intentions of staying maybe six months, or three or four months, you know, like a lot of people I ended up staying. And then I married. I’m married now and I’ve got a little girl five years old.
And so I’m settled. But I don’t work here in San Diego that often. There’s not very much happening here jazz-wise.
So I have to travel, which I don’t mind at all. I don’t mind doing it.
